To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
activation of a cell, activation of an integrins and integrin-cytokine interactions all can affect integrin interactions with the cytoskelelton outside of focal contacts.

1) the alpha-subunit plays an essential role in integrin-cyoskeleton interactions outside of focal contacts, 2) the beta-subunit is also important for these interactions, and 3) activation of the integrins and activation of a cell can affect integrin-ctyskeleton interactions in different ways.

activation of alpha(2)beta(2) and alpha(IIb)-integrin, which are members of the beta(2)-integrin family, results in a decrease in focal contact-independent interactions of the integrins with cytoskeletal elements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the cell's cytoplasmic matrix is linked to the extracellular world.
the mechanisms of cell adhesion and motility.
understanding how integrin-cytokkeleton interactions are regulated.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the alpha-subunit plays an important role in integrin-cytoplasm interactions, and that activation of integrin can be achieved by different mechanisms.
the alpha- and beta-subunits of integrins are equally important for integrin-cytokines interactions.

integrins interact with the actin cytoskeleton in multiple ways, including through the beta-subunit and the alpha-subunit, both in focal contacts and outside of focal contacts, both in activated and in resting states.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

integrins are not simply "molecules" that bind to ligands and to cytoskeleton, but that they are complex structures with multiple domains that can bind to ligands, to cytoskeletal proteins, and to each other, and that these interactions can be regulated in multiple ways.
the alpha-subunit of integrin is a key player for the integrin-cytokkeleton interactions.
the alpha-subunit is a major player in the regulation of integrins, and that it can do this by more than one mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cytoskeleton is an integral component of integrin activation and signaling.
integrin-cytokine interactions are not just important at the focal contacts.
integrin-cytokkeleton interactions are not simply a consequence of the integrin binding ligand, but are also regulated by the state of activation of the integrins.
